title: Sanguszko archive 1662 (catalogue 443): anonymous Polish letter in a composite-group simple substitution, broken from the ciphertext and read

steps.what: DECODE R7513 images (level-2 account) studied at full resolution; atlas of the 23 group shapes frozen before computation.
Front (254 groups) solved by injective annealing on a Polish letter model (Latin, French, German, Italian score lower); g and k corrected from the reading of the front; key frozen.
Held-out reverse (66 groups), one measurement: coverage 0.970; letters in lexicon words 0.864 (segmentation fixed in advance); 200 permuted keys at most 0.576, 200 shuffled texts at most 0.697.
Whole letter read; two single-occurrence groups of the reverse valued from the sense (u, f).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 320 tokens, 24 types, pl-1790 order 4: reading -2.575 per letter; random keys -5.447 (z 10.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.785 (mean -3.887, z 13.3); annealer on the real text -2.865. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.575; polyphony 0.0; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.865

outcome.method_basis: Simple substitution broken from the ciphertext of the front by annealing, validated on the held-out reverse against 200 + 200 controls.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 71/71 words read in their sense; 67 certain (94.4%), 3 probable (4.2%), 1 restored (1.4%), 0 unresolved.

credits.note: ciphertext-only break of the front, validation on the held-out reverse, full reading, English translation
credits.source: email from Brice Dudout to Daniel Bourdeau, 29 Oct 2026; merged from the Dudout bundle (dudout/bundle-ne-colonies), 30 Oct 2026

texts.label: Anonymous letter, 31 July 1662, front and reverse
texts.summary: News from Riga and Hamburg that the Swedes are arming and have ordered prayers and a fast for the third time, a sure sign of war; advice not to leave the side towards the sea bare, since it is far from Lwów to Gdańsk; the Elector will surely come in August.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences from Brice Dudout's reading.md and translation.md (not re-deciphered, not re-checked against the images): three coherent Polish sentences in the spelling of the cipher, with one probable word and one restored letter; the English translation follows the Polish.

prior.where: Catalogue 443 open; research/polish_archives: no key or decryption file on the record; web search on the plaintext phrases (29 Oct 2026): nothing.

human: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
